newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Plavsic may dissolve Bosnian Serb assembly.
newsitem.headline: Plavsic may dissolve Bosnian Serb assembly.

text.p: Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic threatened to dissolve the Serb assembly on Thursday in a letter to her government opponents who have demanded she step down, local television reported.

"I ask you to give me your opinion by 3 p.m. (1300 GMT) on July 3 on the possible dissolution of the people's assembly of the Serb republic," Plavsic was quoted as saying in a letter to Dragan Kalinic, assembly speaker.
The letter cited a constitutional crisis as the basis for a possible presidential order to dissolve the parliament, the television said.
Hardliners loyal to indicted war criminal and ex-president Radovan Karadzic, who dominate the assembly, were preparing to launch proceedings to remove Plavsic at a session scheduled for Friday.
There was no comment on the letter from Plavsic's office in the northern town of Banja Luka, where policemen loyal to the president are guarding her building.
The power struggle in Bosnia's Serb entity between Plavsic and Karadzic's allies erupted over the weekend, when the president called for the suspension of the interior minister, a Karadzic loyalist.

British soldiers in the NATO-led peace force patrolled the streets of Banja Luka overnight to prevent violence from erupting between Plavsic's supporters, who include army generals, and Karadzic's police force.
The ruling Serb Democratic Party nominated Plavsic for the presidency last year in the belief she would prove an obedient successor, but she has condemned the leadership as corrupt war profiteers.
Karadzic, who led separatist Serbs during the 1992-95 war, was forced to step down from office under international pressure last year and promised to stay out of politics.
Scoffing at his indictment by the U.N. war crimes tribunal, Karadzic continues to wield covert influence over his party in a bid to obstruct the peace accords.
Plavsic, herself an ultra-nationalist ideologue, has argued for cooperating with the international community to preserve Serb interests under the U.S.-brokered peace treaty.
